sentences.text: Researchers applied fMRI encoding models using large language model features to examine how brain activity generalizes across language and math tasks in 32 people.
Control analyses suggested that this shared activity might not be fully explained by basic visual processing or general task demands.
Furthermore, analyses of model weights revealed different patterns of neural weighting for shared versus domain-specific predictions.

The brain regions shared across tasks displayed functional connections, a measure of how much the activity of two regions moves together, with language and math networks that depended on the task being performed.
These results suggest that language and math use both partially shared and distinct brain representations.
